sections.h2: Why architecture matters when selling in Miami Beach
sections.html:
The city treats many of its buildings as heritage, and that can limit what a buyer is allowed to change. Miami Beach has the world's largest collection of Art Deco structures, joined by Mediterranean Revival and Miami Modern, or MiMo, designs. The first tropical Art Deco buildings went up in 1933, a few years after the 1926 hurricane forced a round of rebuilding, and a preservation group formed in 1977 to protect the 1930s concentration in South Beach.

Not every block is covered, so the status of one house tells you little about the house two streets over. Find out early whether your lot sits inside a district or carries an individual designation. A buyer planning a renovation will ask, and an answer in hand shortens the negotiation.

The Historic Preservation Board has designation reports for twenty districts and expansions. Several carry the names of familiar streets and neighborhoods.

Individually designated sites include Old City Hall, the Venetian Causeway, the Miami Beach Woman's Club and the 28th Street Obelisk. The city's zoning map and the planning department can tell you which category a given address falls in.

sections.h2: Who approves changes to a historic property?
sections.html:
The seven-member Historic Preservation Board. Its charter powers include issuing or denying certificates of appropriateness, certificates to dig and certificates of appropriateness for demolition inside a district or on a designated site.

  • It reviews new construction, alterations and improvements to designated properties.
  • It prepares guidelines for each site or district that measure whether a proposed change fits.
  • It can recommend restoring property that was altered in violation of the rules.
  • It can grant variances from the land development regulations where hardship is shown.
  • It acts as the city's floodplain management board for applications within its jurisdiction.

The city charter bars weaker preservation standards than those in place on November 6, 2012 unless voters approve. A buyer who dreams of gutting a facade or tearing down a house needs the board's consent, and that uncertainty affects price.

sections.h2: Seawalls and the island's flooding risk
sections.html:
Seawalls are the island's first line of defense against tidal flooding, and the cost of upgrading them falls mostly on private owners. Miami Beach has roughly 55 miles of seawalls, with only about 5 miles publicly owned, so around 91% are private.

For a bayside owner the seawall is part of the property a buyer inspects. Inland owners feel the effects too, because bayside walls decide how far high tides reach into the streets.

  • A January 2021 ordinance requires new seawalls at an elevation of 5.7 feet NAVD 1988 and requires failing seawalls to be rebuilt to that minimum.
  • The city updated the ordinance on July 23, 2025 with revised definitions and construction standards for new and existing barriers.
  • Private owners may qualify for a matching grant for upgrades and for PACE financing through the city's Private Property Adaptation program.

sections.h2: What a bayside seller should prepare
sections.html:
Get an elevation reading and a condition report before you list. The city surveyed seawall elevations citywide and built a tool that lets owners check their vulnerability to rising tides, so start there. A recent survey gives a buyer something concrete and answers the first question a bayfront buyer's agent is likely to ask.

If the wall is below the current minimum or failing, you have two honest paths. Repair it and keep the permits, or disclose the shortfall and let buyers price it. Replacement needs approvals from several agencies, including the federal Army Corps, the state, Miami-Dade County and the city, so build that wait into your timeline. A cash buyer used to waterfront work may accept the job as is, while a financed buyer may need the lender to sign off on the plan.

sections.h2: Can a single-family home be rented by the night?
sections.html:
No. The city's Resiliency Code bars rentals shorter than six months and one day in single-family homes, and in many multi-family buildings in certain zoning districts. Qualifying rentals need a city Business Tax Receipt and a Resort Tax account, and section 102-386 requires both numbers in any advertisement.

The city publishes a list of apartment buildings authorized for short-term rental, and reports of illegal rentals go to Code Compliance. If your past income came from stays the code forbids, expect buyers to value the house as a long-term rental or an owner-occupied home.

sections.h2: Miami-Dade deed tax and closing costs
sections.html:
Miami-Dade charges sixty cents on each $100 and layers a forty-five cent surtax on top, a surtax that skips any deed conveying just a single-family dwelling. Every other Florida county charges 70 cents. The liability falls on everyone named in the deed, and payment goes to the clerk's office with the recording.

Mortgage payoffs, any home equity line, the year's prorated property tax and any condo association estoppel round out the usual closing list.

The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser sets assessments and the county's tax collector bills. Bills arrive in November with a 4% discount that fades to 1% by February, and unpaid bills turn delinquent after April 1.

Selling a homestead ends the exemption on that parcel, and a new owner is assessed at market-based value from the next January 1. If you are moving within Florida, you may carry the saved amount forward by filing for portability by March 1.

An heir needs a court-appointed representative before anyone can deed the house, and a landlord needs a plan for the tenant. Florida's short-form summary administration is open to estates up to $150,000 outside exempt property, or when the death was over two years ago.

For a tenant, a 3-day written demand covers unpaid rent, a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice, and after a court judgment the sheriff posts 24 hours' notice before restoring possession. Decide early whether to deliver the house empty, and keep every notice and receipt. If the mortgage is behind, ask the lender in writing for the payoff and the court case status, since a sale that pays off the lender before the clerk's auction protects any equity.

sections.h2: Cash sale or listing on the Beach
sections.html:
Compare what each route leaves in your pocket. A listing may bring a higher price, but it adds commission, repair requests from the buyer's inspector, months of carrying costs and the risk that a lender balks at a seawall or a historic restriction. A cash buyer used to older Miami Beach buildings will usually take the house as is.

Whichever you choose, get the closing date, deposit and fee split in writing, and do not sign the deed until the contract is final. Pay no fee just to receive an offer.

faqs.q: How many Miami Beach seawalls are on private property?
faqs.a: About 91%. The city counts roughly 55 miles of seawall, of which about 5 miles are publicly owned.

faqs.q: What height must a new Miami Beach seawall reach?
faqs.a: 5.7 feet NAVD 1988 for new seawalls and for failing ones that are rebuilt, under an ordinance that dates to January 2021 and was updated July 23, 2025.

faqs.q: Does the Miami Beach Historic Preservation Board approve demolition?
faqs.a: Yes, inside a historic district or on a designated site. The board issues or denies certificates of appropriateness for demolition.

faqs.q: Is the Miami-Dade deed tax the same as in other counties?
faqs.a: No. Miami-Dade has its own structure, 60 cents per $100 with a 45 cent surtax that does not reach single-family-only deeds, while the rest of Florida pays 70 cents.
